newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 3.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* SBC Communications has filed a lawsuit seeking to overturn provisions in a new telecommunications law restricting Baby Bell sfrom entering long-distance markets.
* The Federal Reserve left untouched its key short-term interest rate.
* The Justice Department approved Raytheon Co's move to acquire the defense system and electronics unit of Texas Instruments Inc on the condition that Raytheon sell a key chip-making operation.
* A computer glitch at Charles Schwab left some of the discount brokerage firm's clients unable to determine whether their trades had been completed.
* General Motors said its U.S. June sales of light vehicles fell 13.5 percent over the prior year.

* Several ex-Prudential Insurance managers have been interviewed by federal authorities investigating possible obstruction of justice in connection with civil suits alleging fraudulent sales practices.
* The New York Stock Exchange is considering eliminating a rule that makes it extremely difficult for listed companies to leave the exchange.
* Rockwell International Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Donald Beall said he was retiring, and is to be succeeded by President and Chief Operating Officer Don Davis.
* General Mills is increasing the price of its breakfast cereals an average of 2.6 percent.
* Tobacco foes are looking to use legislation to preempt cigarette makers by using conclusions of a panel of health experts who are critical of the tobacco settlement.
* Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc said they were open to proposals from LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, which has opposed their possible merger.
* Alliance Capital is forming joint ventures with financial institutions in Brazil, Russian and South Africa.
* Latin stocks are a hot commodity these days, with most major markets up more than 7 percent in June alone.
* The Chicago Merc is considering opening its proposed mini-S&P contract to electronic orders.
* Heard on the Street: The prices of major foreign stocks are showing wide fluctuations on news they are entering or leaving the Morgan Stanley Capital International indexes.
* Credit Markets: Treasury securities posted modest gains, but many market participants were in limbo as they awaited today's U.S. employment report.
